messages.author: ab78e227e394cf1d
messages.subject: Precision parameter of initial value
parts:
Hi INLA group,

I have a good initial guess for inla hyperparameter for log(precision). Now how should I modify corresponding prior?

What should be correct choice for a and b if based on my initial guess with a small sample is tau= 10? How a and b are related with internal initial value of hyperparameter?

```
hyper=list(theta = list(prior = "loggamma",
                                                         param=c(a,b),
                                                         initial=log(10),
                                                         fixed=TRUE)
                                  )

```

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Precision parameter of initial value
parts:
a loggamma(a,b) prior for theta = "log precision", is the same as a Gamma(a,b)
prior for the precision (where E() = a/b).

you normally do not need to change the initial value, as its better for the
optimizer to have a to tight model adapting to data than the other way around.

setting fixed=TRUE, simply treat theta=log(10) as a constant, I guess this is
not what you want.

parts:
it would only help if you fix them. letting them 'close to a spesified value'
might not be very useful, as 'close' is data dependent. use

hyper=list(prec=list(initial=log(value),fixed=TRUE)))

to set precision = value

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Precision parameter of initial value
parts:
no.

initial=a,fixed=T

mean that theta=a and treated as fixed

intial=a,fixed=F

means the initial value=a and treated as random


often user-set intitial values only do worse, as the 'latent' is not aligned, so
it will do worse

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Precision parameter of initial value
parts:
When I have a lot of hyperparameters I would like to vary my hyperparameter around some prespecified value. Based on my small sample application with Eb, I obtained a guess of hyperparamneters. I understand now fixed=TRUE is one option. But I want to keep it random to make it a bit adaptive to the data. Now if I still keep (a=1,b=.005) it is almost flat where initial=10 might not be coming into picture. So my question is should I choose a and b such that a/b=10? 

Otherwise a/b=200 , far away from 10.

Department of Statistics

University of Connecticut

Storrs, CT 06269-4120

On Mon, May 20, 2024 at 1:45 PM Helpdesk (Haavard Rue) <he...@r-inla.org> wrote:
*Message sent from a system outside of UConn.*


no.

initial=a,fixed=T

mean that theta=a and treated as fixed

intial=a,fixed=F

means the initial value=a and treated as random


often user-set intitial values only do worse, as the 'latent' is not aligned, so
it will do worse

On Mon, 2024-05-20 at 13:42 -0400, Alokesh Manna wrote:
